description: Principles that bind executives in emergencies and black-swan events
milestone_2028: Drafted by citizen assemblies and published
milestone_2031: Adopted by vote in regions; executives report against it
milestone_2035: Adopted nationally; every emergency decision is made under it
binding_route: mandate needed; existing powers may suffice
binding_route_note: An executive can adopt the charter under existing powers; statute makes it enforceable

description: Bodies chosen by lot that choose what goes to citizens
milestone_2028: Running in pilot towns and regions
milestone_2031: In every region; first national council
milestone_2035: A national council sets the citizen agenda each year
binding_route_note: A decree or statute gives the council its agenda-setting right, as in Ostbelgien

description: A defined list of decisions that must go to citizens
milestone_2028: List agreed through deliberation, starting from this register
milestone_2031: First reserved decisions made by binding vote, locally and regionally
milestone_2035: National list in law; every decision on it decided or scheduled
citizen_led_start: Opt-in communities bind themselves to citizen decisions
binding_route_note: Statute, or constitutional change where the decisions are constitutionally assigned

description: Every binding vote follows an assembly, and the assembly's wording goes on the ballot
citizen_led_start: Run an assembly before any community vote
binding_route: mandate needed; existing powers may suffice
binding_route_note: A body can adopt the procedure for its own votes; law is needed to require it for every reserved decision

description: A right to overturn a law or executive decision by signatures and a vote
milestone_2028: Designed and debated; used in opt-in communities

description: Panels of affected citizens review every emergency, with all its decisions in reach. Where a decision gives citizens a review power, they also carry out standing reviews and reviews triggered by a major incident
milestone_2028: Citizen-run reviews of recent emergencies and major incidents published
milestone_2031: Review duty accepted by regional agencies
milestone_2035: Automatic for every emergency and every major incident in a reviewed area
binding_route: mandate needed; existing powers may suffice
binding_route_note: Agencies can accept the review duty under existing powers; law is needed to make it automatic everywhere

description: Citizen decisions cannot remove fundamental rights, and courts check this. Every assembly must hear and answer a statement of the effect on future generations
milestone_2028: Floor defined through deliberation, with the rule for future generations
citizen_led_start: Opt-in communities adopt a rights charter
binding_route: mandate needed; existing powers may suffice
binding_route_note: Existing constitutional and court protections may suffice; otherwise statute or constitutional change

description: Open data and AI expert assessment available to every citizen
milestone_2028: Expert service piloted on three decisions, with audit
citizen_led_start: A civil-society service built on open data
binding_route_note: A capability, not an authority. Access to official data may need agency agreement

description: Advisory AI and human mediation for deadlocked citizen bodies
milestone_2028: Piloted under guardrails AX1 to AX8
binding_route_note: Each citizen body adopts it in its own rules

description: Paid time for people chosen by lot, and civic leave
milestone_2028: Stipends in pilots; voluntary civic leave
milestone_2031: Civic leave in workplace agreements and regional rules
citizen_led_start: Employers, co-operatives and philanthropy fund stipends
binding_route_note: Voluntary stipends and leave need no law; a universal right does

description: Skills in deliberation, preparedness, systems thinking and using AI well
milestone_2031: In schools and adult learning across regions
milestone_2035: Most adults have taken part in a deliberation

description: Secure identity, online channels and verifiable votes. Online only by 2035
milestone_2028: Open-source tools piloted; offline channels kept during the transition
milestone_2031: Regional use, audited; assisted online access and an outage rule in place
binding_route: mandate needed; existing powers may suffice
binding_route_note: Tools need no law; legally recognised votes need electoral rules to accept them

description: Representatives and agencies carry out citizen decisions, or the matter returns to citizens
milestone_2028: Public trackers show what was implemented
milestone_2031: Duty to respond in force in regions

description: Democracies and communities recognise each other's citizen processes and decide shared questions together
milestone_2028: A network of opt-in communities across several democracies
milestone_2031: First cross-border citizen decision on a shared resilience question
binding_route_note: Agreement among communities; a treaty to bind states

description: A way for citizens to start and make binding decisions that a later parliament cannot override, outside the constitutional referendum process
milestone_2028: Design agreed through deliberation and the public case made
milestone_2031: Entrenched in at least one state or region
citizen_led_start: Opt-in communities bind themselves; citizens petition for the change
binding_route_note: Must be entrenched so that a later parliament cannot repeal it; an ordinary statute is not enough. In Australia that means constitutional change nationally, and only Parliament can start a referendum
